ci(security): enforce repository trust policy (supersedes #109) (#117)

## What

Daybreak's #109 (`codex/repository-security-policy`, f79b269) with
current `dev` merged in. Merging this closes #109 as merged; its commits
are unchanged.

- `tools/security-policy.mjs` + `tools/security-sinks.json`, run in the
always-on *Tool tests* job: Actions pinned to full SHAs, read-only
workflow defaults, no `pull_request_target`, reviewed executable
rendering sinks (`|raw`, `innerHTML`, `eval`…) by exact inventory, no
tracked generated output, the latest released series marked supported in
`SECURITY.md`, and protected agent rules in `AGENTS.md`.
- `CODEOWNERS`: `@xormania` owns everything, explicitly `.github/`,
`AGENTS.md`, `SECURITY.md` and the policy files.
- `docs/AGENT-ASSURANCE.md`: agent boundaries and a manual adversarial
evaluation protocol. `AGENTS.md`: untrusted-data, credential and
self-approval rules.

## Merge resolution

Two files conflicted with `dev`: `ci.yml` (the Tool tests comment: Jev's
JUnit sentence and the policy sentence, both kept) and `CONTRIBUTING.md`
(the tools/tests row, the docs row with DEMO-SECURITY and
AGENT-ASSURANCE, and the commands list: both sides kept). The policy
passes on the merged tree, including `dev`'s new composite action and
workflows: `node tools/security-policy.mjs` → ok.

## Verification (independent, read-only, on f79b269)

- Policy ok on the head and on hypothetical merges with the shard-plan,
image-digest and modal-fade branches (all since merged).
- Probes: a SHA pin with a version comment passes; `@v4`, `@main`, a
short SHA, a quoted tag pin and `docker://` are caught.

## Checks

- CI on the last commit: pending.
- Locally after the merge: security policy ok, tool tests 156/0,
actionlint, docs-lint, `ci-changes.sh`, llms-txt.
- `CHANGELOG.md` entry: none: repository policy, not the installed kit.

## Owner decisions (CODEOWNERS has no effect by itself)

CODEOWNERS only binds once the `dev` and `main` rulesets require
code-owner review (and, per `docs/AGENT-ASSURANCE.md`, dismiss stale
approvals and allow no bypass). With those settings every PR into `dev`
needs @xormania's approval, including ones an agent opens; GitHub does
not count an author's own approval. Those settings are yours to change;
this PR does not change them.

## Known gaps (accepted, for follow-up)

- Policy false negatives found by the verifier: flow-style `{uses:
…@v4}`, `on: [pull_request_target]` / `on: {pull_request_target: …}`,
`workflow_run`, `${{ github.event.* }}` interpolation in `run:`, and
some sink spellings (`el["innerHTML"]=`, `Function("…")` without `new`,
`setAttribute("srcdoc", …)`). False positives: `permissions: {}` and
`read-all` are refused although safe.
- The sink allowlist matches text and count, not line, so a sink moved
within a file passes.
- The policy runs from the PR's own checkout; CODEOWNERS on the policy
files is the brake.
- The adversarial evaluation table in `docs/AGENT-ASSURANCE.md` is a
manual protocol, not a harness.

specs.title: shows an image that loaded before the controller connected
every button of the default example shows its keyboard focus at 3:1, light theme
arrow, Home, End and Page keys move the focus; right to left swaps the arrows
the month and year dropdowns move the calendar
each mode submits its inputs; day buttons never submit the form
a range never spans a disabled day: a click past one starts a new range
in multiple mode, the inputs keep their attributes and order as dates come and go
under prefers-reduced-motion the chart does not animate
a doughnut colors each slice; a table can be always visible
data-table in a Turbo Frame: sort, page and filter each make one frame request
data-table-live: sort, page and filter each make one Live request
a Live action re-sorting rows makes one request and reconnects each row's dropdown and tooltip once
date-picker: opening and picking a date make no request and leave no listener
measure: a step's duration runs to the frame presented after its update, an expensive frame included
/ answers with the hardening headers and a nonce-based policy its scripts carry
/demo answers with the hardening headers and a nonce-based policy its scripts carry
/demo/login answers with the hardening headers and a nonce-based policy its scripts carry
/lab/live-table answers with the hardening headers and a nonce-based policy its scripts carry
/lab/calendar-turbo answers with the hardening headers and a nonce-based policy its scripts carry
/preview/calendar/default?theme=light answers with the hardening headers and a nonce-based policy its scripts carry
/preview/date-picker/default?theme=light answers with the hardening headers and a nonce-based policy its scripts carry
/preview/editor/default?theme=light answers with the hardening headers and a nonce-based policy its scripts carry
/preview/markdown-editor/default?theme=light answers with the hardening headers and a nonce-based policy its scripts carry
/preview/side-nav/default?theme=light answers with the hardening headers and a nonce-based policy its scripts carry
/lab/mobile-nav answers with the hardening headers and a nonce-based policy its scripts carry
/lab/modal-turbo answers with the hardening headers and a nonce-based policy its scripts carry
every response gets its own nonces
the layout sets the theme before the first paint
ArrowDown in the field opens the calendar; a range closes after both ends
on a desktop the navbar menu marks the current page, opens its submenus and visits their links
on a phone the drawer holds the sidebar navigation, then the navbar menu
the not-found block answers 404 and passes axe
the dashboard passes axe at phone width, its channel bars are meters
flash messages show on every layout: the logout notice on the auth layout, not later on the dashboard
every layout keeps the same toast region: a toast closed on another layout does not come back on Back
every page of the gallery and of the demo names an icon, so a browser asks for no /favicon.ico
